newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil extends losses at close.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil extends losses at close.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL
May (3rd pos) 1,268 rgt/tonne Mar (south) 1,317.50
Open/Hi/Low 1,265/1,273/1,261 Prev close 1,337.50
Prev settlement 1,275 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES-Prices drifted in afternoon before closing lower after talk that Pakistan private sectors were in the market as re-sellers, technical and plantation selling coupled with losses in soyoil. SGS's Feb 1-25 export data has no impact. May futures fell to 1,261 low, next support 1,250
PALM OIL PHYSICAL- Interest was mostly seen among products and nearby CPOs. Selling was seen on lack of export demand.

The Malaysian palm oil market drifted in late choppy trading before closing a shade lower after talk that Pakistan private sector were in the market as re-sellers, and as technical selling and soyoil losses dampened sentiment, traders said.

News that cargo surveyor SGS Sdn Bhd put February 1-25 exports at 360,382 tonnes against 401,932 in the same period of January, were within estimates and had no market impact. "There were a lot of uncertainties in the afternoon. The market was choppy particularly in late trading. People were unsure of the path." a trader said.
"At the upper side, there were plantation and dealers selling, while at the lower end, speculative buying, bargain hunting and shortcovering were seen," the trader said.
Talk that Pakistan private sectors were in the market as resellers had sparked off selling this morning, they said, but they could not confirm the speculation.

"Pakistan has been buying little these days and mainly from hand-to-mouth basis. Whatever they buy its mostly for prompt shipment," a Malaysian trader said. He said it was unlikely for Pakistan to resell the oil.

Pakistani vegetable oil traders said on Tuesday they were unaware of any palm oil reselling by local dealers, as rumoured in London. Prices on the European market were also pulled down by this rumour on Monday, traders said.

Technical sentiment was bearish and May futures continued to fall after it broke 1,290 ringgit on Monday. "There was further selling technically and May futures would see the next support at 1,250 ringgit," another trader said.
At the close, May futures contract fell seven ringgit at 1,268 ringgit ($511.39) a tonne after moving in a band of 1,261 and 1,273 level.
Physicals also saw some selling activities on talk of the Pakistan reselling, traders said.

Physical Mar (south) crude palm oil was offered 1,317.50 ringgit against bids of 1,315 with earlier trades done at 1,315 and 1,320. Mar (central) saw offers at 1,312.50 and bids at 1,307.50 and Mar (north) at 1,305 against bids 1,295.
Apr (south) was offered at 1,307.50 with bids at 1,305 after trading at 1,310 and 1,305. Apr (central) saw offers at 1,300 with bids at 1,290.
Among refined products, Mar RBD palm oil was offered at $562.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Apr at $555 and May/Jun at $550. Mar was traded at $558, $559 and $560.
Mar RBD palm olein saw offers at $587.50, Apr at $577.50 and Apr/May/Jun at $572.50. Mar was dealt at $584, $585, Apr at $576, $577.50 and May at $572.50.
Mar RBD palm stearin was offered at $465 and Mar/Apr palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $310.
